## Recall · Lecture 7

a) Which computer does an iOS build need?
b) Why does an Android launch need more test phones?
c) Which source is best for a fact about iOS?

::: {.answer}
a) a Mac with Xcode
b) fragmentation: many makers and models
c) Apple's own page, with its date
:::

## Activity 1 · Four rows · 15 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Star Garden is made by two friends with one Windows laptop, two Android phones and no Mac.
- **Do it:** Fill a table for Android and iOS with four rows: build computer, test phones, installing and updates. Write a source with its date in every row.
- Your product is a table with four rows.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/comparison-table.png)
:::
::::

## Check 1 · Four rows

What does a good comparison table contain?

::: {.reveal}
1. Build computer: any PC for Android, a Mac with Xcode for iOS.
2. Test phones: several Android models, but only a few iPhones.
3. Installing: stores and .apk files on Android, the App Store on iOS.
4. Updates come from each maker on Android, and from Apple for all iPhones at once.
:::

## Check 2 · Sort and advise

What are the right sorts and good advice?

::: {.reveal}
1. "An iOS build needs a Mac" is an official fact from Apple's developer pages.
2. "7 in 10 phones run Android" changes, so it needs a dated report.
3. "Android games are always slower" and "iPhones cannot get viruses" are myths.
4. Good advice: launch on Android first, because the studio has no Mac; add iOS when it can rent a Mac.
:::

## Wrap-up

- You can compare two platforms in a table with a dated source in every row.
- You can tell facts from myths and write advice with what, why and what would change it.
